question: What is the main goal of taking a nutritional supplement?

options.A: To add extra dietary ingredients to a person's daily intake
options.B: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.C: To completely replace the need for eating solid foods
options.D: To act as a prescribed pharmaceutical medication

explanation: Supplements are meant to add to your normal meals, not replace them! They give your body a little extra boost of vitamins or minerals when needed.

question: Why should nurses always ask patients about any supplements they are taking?

options.A: Supplements are always provided free of charge by the hospital pharmacy
options.B: Doctors prescribe them for every single diagnosis upon admission
options.C: Patients often take them independently and they can impact overall health
options.D: Hospitals require patients to stop all eating and only take supplements

explanation: Many people buy and take supplements on their own without telling anyone. As a nurse, asking about them helps you keep an eye on everything entering the patient's body!

question: Which group of vitamins is known as fat-soluble?

options.A: Vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.B: Vitamin C and the B-complex group

explanation: Think of vitamins A, D, E, and K as the ones that dissolve in fat and can hang out in our body's fatty tissues and liver for later use.

question: How are minerals fundamentally different from vitamins?

options.A: Minerals are only found in pills, while vitamins come from plants
options.B: Minerals are inorganic elements, whereas vitamins are organic compounds
options.C: Minerals provide energy calories, whereas vitamins do not
options.D: Minerals dissolve in fat, whereas vitamins dissolve in water

explanation: Minerals like iron and calcium come straight from the earth and water (inorganic), whereas vitamins are made by living things (organic). Easy to remember once you link minerals to rocks and soil!

question: Which supplement is given to pregnant women to help prevent neural tube defects?
explanation: Folic acid is a super important vitamin during early pregnancy. It helps the baby's brain and spinal cord develop properly.

question: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet and avoids all animal products is most at risk of lacking which nutrient?
explanation: Vitamin B12 is mostly found in animal foods like meat, eggs, and dairy. Strict vegans often need to take a supplement to keep their B12 levels healthy.

question: What is the most reliable way to check if a patient actually has a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Asking the patient what they ate yesterday
options.B: Observing the color of the patient's skin

explanation: Lab tests give us clear, factual proof of what's inside the patient's blood, helping us avoid guessing or giving supplements they don't need.

question: Why can it be tricky to diagnose a nutrition problem based only on general tiredness?

options.A: Patients always exaggerate how tired they feel
options.B: Fatigue can be caused by many non-nutritional health conditions
options.C: Nutrient deficiencies never cause tiredness or weakness
options.D: Fatigue only occurs when a person is completely dehydrated

explanation: Feeling tired is a sign of many things—like lack of sleep, stress, or an infection—not just poor food intake. We have to look at the whole picture!

question: Which type of vitamin can easily build up to toxic levels if taken in excess over time?
explanation: Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in body fat instead of being peed out quickly, taking too many of them over time can lead to a harmful buildup.

question: What is a major risk when a patient takes herbal supplements along with their regular prescription drugs?

options.A: Herbs always neutralize all side effects of drugs
options.C: The prescription drugs will become completely odorless
options.D: The medications will instantly turn into sugar

explanation: Herbs are active chemicals too! When mixed with hospital drugs, they can sometimes clash, making the drugs too strong or blocking them from working.

question: What important advice should you give a patient who wants to start taking a daily multivitamin?

options.A: Taking five times the recommended dose will speed up healing
options.B: Natural supplements never interact with prescribed heart medications
options.C: Supplements do not replace the benefits of eating a balanced, whole-food diet
options.D: There is no need to tell the doctor about over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Real, whole foods give our bodies natural fiber and nutrients that pills just cannot completely copy. Supplements are helpers, not food substitutes!

question: Which of these is a bad practice when choosing a nutritional supplement?

options.A: Following the recommended dosage instructions on the bottle
options.B: Ignoring product labels and ingredient lists completely
options.C: Buying products verified by independent quality testing
options.D: Checking with a healthcare provider before starting

explanation: Always read the label! Ignoring it means you might miss allergy warnings, wrong dosages, or hidden ingredients.
